title: Nearest Postcode From Your List Finder
description: Rank up to 50 UK postcodes or US ZIPs by straight-line distance from your chosen point.
summary_sentence: Rank resolved representative postcode points, not exact addresses or road journeys.
quick_answer: Enter a target point and up to 50 full UK postcodes or five-digit US ZIPs. The tool requests representative coordinates from postcodes.io or Zippopotam and ranks successfully resolved codes by spherical distance. Unmatched codes are omitted, so check the returned list.

body.t: Compare candidate depot postcodes by straight-line distance. Confirm the actual depot address and road route before making an assignment.

faq: US ZIPs or UK postcodes — both?
Both families are the tool's home ground, matched within whichever list you paste. Mixed lists rank together once each code resolves to its centroid.
What if a code on my list cannot be found?
Unmatched, unsupported or failed lookups are omitted without an individual report. Compare your input list with the output before relying on it.
This finder ranks by straight-line (centroid) distance — the fast, explainable rule. Road-nearest is the routing family's different answer; for close calls, check the winner by road.
How many codes can the list hold?
The current workspace accepts at most 50 entries per run.
One point per query here — the assignment question is per-customer by nature. Batch assignment belongs to a spreadsheet or GIS wearing this same distance rule.
Resolved results are listed by distance. Displayed rounding can make nearby values look equal; the tool does not provide a special tie policy.
Why not just use the single nearest postcode tool?
Because your network is the constraint. The generic nearest ignores your depots; this finder's list is the business logic, and the geometry serves it.
